featured_reviews.name: brendan fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very disappointing experience at Shanti Book Store. When I went to buy books, they offered used books, claiming they were “unused,” and sold them at a discounted price. Later, when I took my daughter’s old books to sell, they offered me only ₹100. After that, I noticed the same books were being sold to other parents at a much higher price (around half of the MRP).
This feels unfair and misleading. I request that other parents be careful while buying or selling books here. The old man who handles it is a very cheap beggar. When I said that I am taking my old books back then he took out some books giving them back to me and says this is no longer in use school has stopped this edition and u feel that it is not in use. This is all about a scam. Parents be alert.

featured_reviews.name: Aditya Chadha
featured_reviews.review_text: They host wonderful events, but even more importantly, the staff are an absolute pleasure. I was looking for a book by a particular author and, after some disappointing experiences at another popular bookshop in Bandra, I was genuinely nervous about asking for help. At that other store (which rhymes with “confectionery”), the staff were often rude and surprisingly unfamiliar with many authors. When I cautiously approached the desk, the two gentlemen working there were incredibly kind, helpful, and immediately knew exactly who I was talking about. Their warmth and knowledge made all the difference. On top of that, they have a fantastic selection of books and authors. A truly lovely bookstore.

featured_reviews.review_text: Here for a literary festival. Nice ambience, helpful staff. Good to see my books displayed!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Most beautiful book store I ever visited.
You enter inside title waves and it's just you and world of books.
I really appreciate such a beautiful place located in bandra.
It's also have small cute small cafe guys I just can't tell in words how beautiful this place is!!
To know more  or want to explore the experience by yourself than please visit this Best place to purchase your next book.

featured_reviews.name: Jaimine BezBoznik Blesav
featured_reviews.review_text:
Highly recommended for non-fiction readers, researchers, thinkers, and anyone who enjoys meaningful reading beyond trends and algorithms.

Title Waves in Bandra has one of the finest collections across geopolitics, history, psychology, philosophy, business, biographies, and contemporary world affairs. The atmosphere is calm, intellectual, and welcoming for readers who still believe in the joy of physically browsing bookshelves.

A perfect place to disconnect from digital noise and reconnect with ideas, perspectives, and conversations that genuinely stimulate the mind.

featured_reviews.name: Architect on Trails
featured_reviews.review_text:
This cozy bookstore stands out for its unique selection. So many books I’ve never seen elsewhere! The vibe is just right for losing track of time among the shelves. There's also a café and a few seats next to the central podium.

A must-visit for anyone who loves books and cafés. Five stars for the variety!

featured_reviews.name: Nida Sayed Kadri
featured_reviews.review_text:
Misleading pricing, zero customer service, and shockingly rude behaviour — absolutely not worth the visit.

I visited this shop to purchase (not rent) a complete book series and clearly explained my requirement at the very start. The owner initially seemed pleased when he heard I wanted to buy. Instead of helping, he asked me to search through a stack of books and said he would remove the set if I found it.

I found one part of the series myself and asked him to look for the remaining books. He completely ignored the request. When I asked for the price of the entire set, he quoted an amount which I felt was reasonable for a second-hand paperback. However, when I again asked for the remaining books, he suddenly said that price was for just one book, not the full set.

I calmly mentioned that a brand-new set online costs one-fourth of what he was asking for a single second-hand copy. That’s when things turned ugly. He got irritated, raised his voice, and when I politely asked why the pricing was so high, he became openly aggressive and started yelling.

He even accused me of “wasting his effort” saying “itni mehnat karayi, kaam karwaya ab book nahi leni” — which is absurd, considering I was there for barely 5 minutes and had found the book myself from the first stack. Neither he nor his staff made any effort to help.

I finally told him that he needs to learn basic manners while dealing with customers.

If this shop believes that once a book is shown, purchasing is mandatory, then they should put up a clear sign outside. Until then, be prepared for rude behaviour, misleading pricing, and zero customer courtesy.

featured_reviews.name: Shaikh Zeeshan
featured_reviews.review_text:
If there’s a list of things to do in Mumbai, visiting and buying books from Flora Fountain’s book street would be a must. Every morning at 10 am, the blue plastic sheets are removed from the stacks of books making every human around look like dwarfs. The sellers take their places and start calling out to passersby like the vendors you see in any local market. They’ll ask what kind of books you are looking for and what genre or writer is that you are in awe of, and the moment you tell them, they’ll definitely get something for you.

This iconic book street is standing tall for the last 60 years and is definitely a heaven for all book lovers. From the classics to new bestsellers, from fiction to non-fiction, poetry to academic, originals to secondhand books, Flora’s book street has everything right on its stacks.

Popularly and fondly known as ‘Book Street Center’ by its visitors, this stretch of the pavement runs right opposite the gorgeous Flora Fountain. Calling these stacks as stacks would definitely be an understatement as it’s more like massive walls of books. Some vendors have even arranged them in a way that it feels like you’re standing inside a box of books.

Another thing that makes this book street iconic is the price at which the books are available. You can find children’s books starting from just Rs.10, while a copy of books, can be purchased at just Rs.1000. All such books otherwise will cost you at least a thousand rupees online. The sellers are polite and well-versed with each and every book they have, and they will be more than happy to help you.

featured_reviews.name: Kusal Rai
featured_reviews.review_text: Tucked away in an aesthetic corner of South Bombay, this bookstore is a true haven for book lovers. With its charming atmosphere and thoughtfully curated shelves, it offers an impressive range of genres that caters to every kind of reader. Whether you’re hunting for a classic, exploring contemporary fiction, or diving into niche subjects, this place makes browsing feel like an experience rather than just a visit. A must-stop spot for any book nerd wandering through the city.

featured_reviews.name: Anil Bishnoi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ashish Book Centre, tucked away near the bustling CSMT Railway Station in Fort, is nothing short of a paradise for true book lovers. In a city that’s always racing against time, this bookstore feels like a quiet, timeless refuge where stories patiently wait to be discovered.

What makes Ashish Book Centre truly special is its incredible collection. From rare second-hand classics and academic textbooks to novels, competitive exam guides, and out-of-print treasures—you never know what gem you’ll stumble upon. Browsing through the shelves feels like going on a literary treasure hunt, and every visit brings a new surprise.

The owners and staff are extremely knowledgeable and helpful. They don’t just sell books; they understand them. Whether you walk in with a specific title in mind or just a vague idea of what you want to read, they guide you with genuine enthusiasm and honesty. Their passion for books is infectious.

Another big win is the affordability. Ashish Book Centre proves that great reading doesn’t have to be expensive. Students, avid readers, and collectors alike will appreciate the fair pricing and excellent condition of the books.

Located in the heart of Fort, just a stone’s throw from CSMT, it’s incredibly convenient and perfectly placed for a spontaneous visit after work or college. Despite the chaos outside, the store offers a calm, almost nostalgic vibe that reminds you why physical bookstores still matter.

If you love books, value knowledge, or simply enjoy the charm of old-school bookstores, Ashish Book Centre is an absolute must-visit. It’s not just a shop—it’s an experience, a legacy, and a reminder that the love for reading is very much alive in Mumbai. 📚
